title: Photosynthesis: Energy Conversion and Carbon Flow
sourceLabel: 既存教材をTOEFL形式へ変換 · 元の問1–9に対応
verificationNote: 四つの原文段落と全九つの学習対象を保持し、元の記述問題を英語四択へ変換しました。

passages.text:
Photosynthesis is often compressed into one balanced equation, but an equation hides the sequence that makes the conversion possible. In oxygenic photosynthesis, pigments absorb photons and transfer excitation energy within organized protein complexes. Reaction centers then initiate electron transfer. Water supplies replacement electrons; its oxidation releases protons and molecular oxygen. Thus, the oxygen released to the atmosphere comes from water, whereas much of the carbon in newly formed organic matter comes from carbon dioxide.

The light reactions do not manufacture a finished sugar in one step. Electron transport helps build a proton gradient across a membrane, and that gradient drives ATP synthesis. Electrons also reduce NADP+ to NADPH. ATP and NADPH are temporary carriers: one supplies usable chemical energy and the other reducing power. Calling them “stored sunlight” is a helpful shorthand only if we remember that the phrase describes transformed energy, not trapped light.

Carbon fixation begins when an enzyme incorporates carbon dioxide into an organic pathway. The Calvin–Benson cycle uses ATP and NADPH and produces three-carbon compounds that can feed many metabolic routes. Some carbon contributes to sugars, starch, cellulose, lipids, or amino acids; some returns to the atmosphere through respiration. It is therefore more accurate to describe photosynthesis as part of a coupled carbon economy than as a factory that outputs glucose alone.

At planetary scale, photosynthetic organisms support food webs and have transformed atmospheric chemistry. Yet gross carbon uptake is not the same as long-term carbon storage. Respiration, decomposition, fire, harvest, and ocean exchange return carbon on different timescales. A forest can be highly productive without storing every absorbed carbon atom permanently. Careful reading follows both the flow of energy and the residence time of matter.

questions.prompt: What is the main idea of the passage?

options.label: A
options.text: A single equation is enough to explain every mechanism of photosynthesis.

options.label: B
options.text: Photosynthesis should be understood by tracing energy conversion, atomic sources, and later carbon flows.

options.label: C
options.text: Plants permanently store every carbon atom they absorb.

options.label: D
options.text: ATP is a container filled with unchanged sunlight.

questions.answer: 正解：B。エネルギー変換、原子の由来、炭素の後続経路を追うことが主題です。Aは反応順序、Cは戻り流、Dはエネルギー変換を無視します。

questions.prompt: What are the principal sources of released oxygen and carbon in newly formed organic matter?

options.label: A
options.text: Oxygen comes from water oxidation, while organic carbon comes mainly from carbon dioxide fixation.

options.label: B
options.text: Both oxygen and carbon come only from soil minerals.

options.label: C
options.text: Atmospheric oxygen comes from splitting carbon dioxide, while carbon comes from water.

options.label: D
options.text: Neither water nor carbon dioxide supplies atoms to the products.

questions.answer: 正解：A。放出酸素は水の酸化、有機物の炭素は主に二酸化炭素固定に由来します。B～Dは原子の移動元を取り違えます。

questions.prompt: The word “shorthand” in paragraph 2 is closest in meaning to

options.label: A
options.text: a deliberately false claim

options.label: B
options.text: a compact expression that omits detail

options.label: C
options.text: an experimental control

options.label: D
options.text: a permanent chemical store

questions.answer: 正解：B。詳細を省いて情報を圧縮する便利な表現です。「stored sunlight」は変換された化学エネルギーを指し、光そのものを閉じ込める意味ではありません。

questions.prompt: How does the proton gradient contribute to ATP synthesis?

options.label: A
options.text: Light-driven electron transport creates an electrochemical gradient across a membrane, which ATP synthase uses.

options.label: B
options.text: Photons are poured directly into ATP molecules without electron transport.

options.label: C
options.text: The gradient destroys all membrane organization before ATP can form.

options.label: D
options.text: ATP synthesis occurs without any energy-transducing intermediate.

questions.answer: 正解：A。光で始まる電子伝達が膜を隔てた勾配を作り、ATP合成酵素が利用します。B～Dはエネルギー変換の因果順序を消します。

questions.prompt: Why does the passage reject the description of photosynthesis as a factory producing only glucose?

options.label: A
options.text: The cycle produces three-carbon compounds that enter many pathways, and fixed carbon can form diverse molecules or return through respiration.

options.label: B
options.text: The Calvin–Benson cycle directly produces only finished glucose and nothing else.

options.label: C
options.text: Fixed carbon cannot enter starch, cellulose, lipids, or amino acids.

options.label: D
options.text: Respiration never returns carbon to the atmosphere.

questions.answer: 正解：A。直接産物は多経路へ入る三炭素化合物で、糖、構造物質、脂質、アミノ酸になり、呼吸で戻る分もあります。B～Dは炭素経済を単純化します。

questions.prompt: Which inference is best supported by the passage?

options.label: A
options.text: Light-independent reactions never depend on products made using light.

options.label: B
options.text: High gross uptake alone proves permanent carbon storage.

options.label: C
options.text: Photosynthetic products enter several metabolic and structural pathways.

options.label: D
options.text: Atmospheric oxygen is released by splitting carbon dioxide.

questions.answer: 正解：C。固定炭素は多様な代謝・構造経路へ入ります。AはATP・NADPH依存、Bは吸収と貯留、Dは酸素原子の由来を誤ります。

questions.prompt: Why can a highly productive forest fail to store every absorbed carbon atom for the long term?

options.label: A
options.text: Respiration, decomposition, fire, and harvest return carbon, and different pools have different residence times.

options.label: B
options.text: Gross uptake and permanent storage are always identical.

options.label: C
options.text: Carbon leaves no biological pool once it is fixed.

options.label: D
options.text: Storage depends only on uptake and never on outflows.

questions.answer: 正解：A。呼吸、分解、火災、収穫による流出があり、貯留場所ごとに滞留時間も異なります。B～Dは炭素収支の流出側を無視します。

questions.prompt: What distinction is made between energy flow and the residence time of matter?

options.label: A
options.text: Energy flow traces movement and transformation, while residence time asks how long matter remains in a pool.

options.label: B
options.text: Both terms mean only the instantaneous rate of photon absorption.

options.label: C
options.text: Residence time measures the color of pigments rather than carbon storage.

options.label: D
options.text: Energy flow proves that matter remains permanently in one place.

questions.answer: 正解：A。flowは移動・変換経路、residence timeは物質が貯留場所に残る長さを問います。B～Dは異なる問いを混同します。

questions.prompt: Which revision best corrects the claim that adding plants permanently stores all absorbed carbon?

options.label: A
options.text: More vegetation may raise uptake, but net durable storage depends on baseline additionality, respiration, decomposition, fire, harvest, soils, and reversal risk.

options.label: B
options.text: Every absorbed atom is permanently removed regardless of later pathways.

options.label: C
options.text: Carbon uptake should be reported without storage duration or outflows.

options.label: D
options.text: Fire and decomposition cannot affect a vegetation project's carbon balance.

questions.answer: 正解：A。吸収増と永久貯留を分け、追加性、流出、滞留期間、反転リスク、生態系影響を条件に含めます。B～Dは総吸収を永続貯留と同一視します。
